access_evidence: probe pubmed_eutils_esearch: HTTP 200, DOI resolves via the [doi] field tag; probe pubmed_eutils_efetch: HTTP 200 with ArticleIdList carrying doi/pubmed/pmc/mid IdTypes. 3 chunked esearch calls over 60 DOIs resolved 37 distinct PMIDs; one efetch returned all 37.
blockers: DOIs must be double-quoted before the [doi] tag: an unquoted 60-DOI OR query silently returned 10 of 37 hits because PubMed's parser splits on the embedded '/' and '('.
historical_depth: No record-creation or index timestamp is exposed, so PubMed can only ever supply a current-snapshot date.
licence_note: NLM makes PubMed citation data available for public use and the E-utilities usage policy grants keyless access at <=3 req/s (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25497/). No blanket content licence is attached to the citation metadata and abstract copyright stays with the publisher, so this is open_no_explicit_licence.
name: PubMed E-utilities
notes: PubMed is not a superset of Europe PMC and vice versa, but on this sample the two agree on 37 PMIDs exactly and disagree on publication date for only 3 of 37 pairs.
rate_policy: NCBI policy: <=3 requests/second without an API key. Used at 1 req/s with tool= and email= set. A key raises the limit but is not required.
robots_summary: Not applicable: E-utilities only, no HTML scraping.
what_is_new: Provides the authoritative PMID<->DOI edge and the GrantList (7 of 37 records). Its PMID set matches OpenAlex's pmid field exactly (37 vs 37), which is a clean independent cross-check of the identifier links.
